title: National Party Wins Election, Begins Economic Reform
notes: Jim Bolger's National won a landslide in 1990 and pursued deregulation and welfare reform. Confirmed.

title: Employment Contracts Act Transforms Labour Relations
notes: ECA passed 15 May 1991, replaced collective bargaining with individual contracts, union membership collapsed. Confirmed.

title: Benefit Cuts Trigger Poverty Surge
notes: Ruth Richardson's 'Mother of All Budgets' 1991 cut benefits by up to 25%. Confirmed.

title: Sealord Fisheries Deal Advances Maori Economic Rights
notes: Deed of Settlement signed 23 September 1992; $170 million total value including Sealord stake and quota. Confirmed.

title: MMP Electoral System Adopted by Referendum
notes: Binding referendum 6 November 1993; 53.9% voted for MMP. Confirmed.

title: Fiscal Responsibility Act Sets Government Budget Framework
notes: FRA passed 1994, came into force 1 July 1994. Internationally recognised as pioneering. Confirmed.

title: Tainui Raupatu Settlement Marks Treaty Justice Milestone
notes: Deed of Settlement signed 22 May 1995; $170 million compensation. Confirmed as first major iwi-level settlement.

title: New Zealand Protests French Nuclear Tests at Mururoa
notes: France resumed testing September 1995; NZ sent naval vessel Tui, PM Bolger and Helen Clark both participated. Ambassador protest confirmed.

title: First MMP Election Produces Coalition Government
notes: First MMP election 12 October 1996; Winston Peters chose National coalition on 10 December 1996. Confirmed.

title: Ngai Tahu Treaty Settlement Signed
notes: Deed of Settlement signed 21 November 1997; $170 million compensation; Aoraki/Mt Cook return confirmed.

title: Helen Clark Becomes Prime Minister, Labour Returns to Power
notes: Clark won 1999 election, formed coalition with Alliance (Jim Anderton as Deputy PM). She was second female PM but first elected as such — description calling her 'second female prime minister' is accurate.

title: Air New Zealand Government Bailout Averts Collapse
notes: NZ$885 million rescue package; government took 80-82% ownership after Ansett Australia collapse. Confirmed.

title: New Zealand Refuses to Join Iraq War Coalition
notes: Clark government declined to join without UN Security Council mandate. Confirmed.

title: Supreme Court Established, Privy Council Jurisdiction Ends
notes: Supreme Court Act passed 17 October 2003; came into force 1 January 2004. Note: description says 162 years of appeals — NZ became a dominion in 1907 and appeals began earlier; approximate figure acceptable.

title: Foreshore and Seabed Act Sparks Maori Protest
notes: Act passed November 2004; hikoi of up to 15,000 arrived at Parliament May 2004; led to formation of Maori Party. Confirmed.

title: New Zealand Signs Closer Economic Partnership with China
notes: NZ was first developed country to recognise China as market economy; formal FTA negotiations announced November 2004, first round December 2004. Event places this at 2005 — negotiations were ongoing in 2005. Broadly accurate.

title: Anti-Terror Raids in Urewera Ranges Target Activists
notes: October 2007 raids; 18 arrested; terrorism charges later dropped; firearms convictions only. Confirmed.

title: NZ-China Free Trade Agreement First for a Developed Nation
notes: FTA signed 7 April 2008; first comprehensive FTA China signed with a developed/OECD country. Confirmed.

title: John Key Leads National to Election Victory
notes: National won 2008 election; John Key became PM, ending nine years of Labour government. Confirmed.

title: Canterbury Earthquake Damages Christchurch
notes: Magnitude 7.1 (not 7.1 as stated — GeoNet records it as 7.2, but 7.1 is the commonly reported figure); struck near Darfield 4 September 2010; no direct fatalities. Confirmed.

title: Christchurch Earthquake Kills 185 in Deadliest Disaster
notes: Magnitude 6.3; 22 February 2011; 185 deaths; CTV building collapse. Confirmed.

title: Canterbury Earthquake Recovery Authority Established
notes: CERA established 2011 with extraordinary powers including compulsory acquisition; residential red zones created. Confirmed.

title: Pike River Mine Disaster Inquiry Begins
notes: Pike River explosion killed 29 miners November 2010; Royal Commission inquiry began 2011. Event year 2011 for the inquiry is correct.

title: New Zealand Signs Wellington Declaration with United States
notes: Title is wrong: the Wellington Declaration was signed in 2010, not 2012. In 2012 New Zealand signed the Washington Declaration on Defence Cooperation. Year and title are mismatched — materially wrong.

title: Marriage Equality Legislation Passed
notes: Marriage (Definition of Marriage) Amendment Act passed 17 April 2013; 13th country globally and first in Asia-Pacific. Maori love song sung in gallery. Confirmed.

title: GCSB Surveillance Powers Expanded Amid Controversy
notes: GCSB Amendment Act passed 2013 after illegal surveillance revelations including Kim Dotcom. Confirmed.

title: Fonterra Botulism Contamination Scare Hits Dairy Exports
notes: Fonterra botulism scare occurred August 2013, not 2014. Year off by 1.

title: New Zealand Flag Referendum Launched
notes: Two-stage referendum process launched 2015; first vote Nov/Dec 2015; second vote March 2016 retained existing flag; $26 million cost confirmed.

title: Trans-Pacific Partnership Agreement Signed
notes: TPP was signed on 4 February 2016 in Auckland, not 2015. Year is off by 1.

title: Kaikoura Earthquake Disrupts South Island Infrastructure
notes: Magnitude 7.8; 14 November 2016; 2 deaths; severed road and rail links; raised seabed confirmed. Confirmed.

title: Jacinda Ardern Becomes Youngest Female Head of Government
notes: Ardern sworn in 26 October 2017, age 37; world's youngest female head of government at the time; coalition with NZ First and Greens. Confirmed.

title: Wellbeing Budget Framework Announced
notes: Ardern government announced Wellbeing Budget approach in 2018 for the 2019 budget; NZ first Western nation to structure budget around wellbeing indicators. Confirmed.

title: Five Eyes Tensions as NZ Balances China and US Relations
notes: Five Eyes Huawei 5G tensions and NZ's balancing act between China and US well-documented in 2018. Confirmed.

title: Christchurch Mosque Attacks Kill 51 in Mass Shooting
notes: 15 March 2019; 51 killed; 40 injured; white supremacist attacker; two mosques. Confirmed.

title: Assault Weapons Banned Within Weeks of Mosque Attack
notes: Arms Amendment Act passed within 26 days; 56,000+ firearms collected in buyback. Confirmed.

title: Whakaari/White Island Eruption Kills 22 Tourists
notes: 9 December 2019 phreatic eruption; 22 deaths; 47 people on island; mostly tourists including Australians. Confirmed.

title: Zero Carbon Act Sets Climate Change Targets
notes: Climate Change Response (Zero Carbon) Amendment Act 2019; net-zero by 2050; independent Climate Change Commission established. Confirmed.

title: COVID-19 Elimination Strategy and Strict Border Closure
notes: NZ implemented elimination strategy and strict border closure March 2020; internationally praised. Confirmed.

title: Ardern Wins Landslide Re-election Under MMP
notes: Labour won 65 of 120 seats on 17 October 2020; first single-party majority under MMP. Confirmed.

title: Housing Crisis Declared as Prices Surge
notes: Housing affordability crisis formally acknowledged 2021; investor deductibility removal and foreign buyer ban introduced. Confirmed.

title: AUKUS Pact Announced Without New Zealand Inclusion
notes: AUKUS announced September 2021; NZ excluded due to nuclear-free legislation. Confirmed.

title: New Zealand Shifts to Living with COVID After Delta Outbreak
notes: Delta outbreak August 2021 prompted pivot from elimination to vaccine-based suppression approach. Confirmed.

title: Anti-Mandate Protest Occupies Parliament Grounds
notes: Parliament grounds occupation ended in police clearance 2 March 2022; anti-vaccine mandate protest. Confirmed.

title: Jacinda Ardern Resigns as Prime Minister
notes: Ardern announced resignation January 2023; stated she lacked energy to continue. Confirmed.

title: Cyclone Gabrielle Causes Worst Flooding in Decades
notes: February 2023; 11 deaths; national state of emergency declared; damage estimated NZ$9-14.5 billion (event states $13.5B, within range). Confirmed.

title: Christopher Luxon Leads National-ACT-NZ First Coalition
notes: October 2023 election; Luxon formed three-party coalition with ACT and NZ First. Confirmed.

title: Treaty Principles Bill Sparks Nationwide Maori Protests
notes: Treaty Principles Bill introduced 2024; nine-day hikoi to Parliament November 2024; 42,000 at Parliament. Bill subsequently defeated at second reading. Confirmed.

title: Government Reverses Smokefree 2025 Legislation
notes: Luxon government repealed Smokefree legislation; internationally criticised by public health advocates. Confirmed.
